9 ابلقّ , inf. n. اِبْلِقَاقٌ; (IDrd, S, K;) and ↓ ابلاقّ , (IDrd, K,) inf. n. اِبْلِيقَاقٌ; (IDrd, TA;) and ↓ ابلولق , inf. n. اِبْلِيلَاقٌ; (TA;) and ↓ بَلِقَ , aor.
بَلَقَ , (JK, K,) inf. n. بَلقٌ; (K, * TA; [accord. to the CK بَلقٌ, but this is a mistake;]) and ↓ بَلُقَ , aor.
بَلُقَ ; (K;) but IDrd asserts only the first and second of these verbs to be known; (TA;) He (a horse) was, or became, ابلق, i. e., black and white: (S, K:) or white in the kind legs as high as the thighs. (K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
